answer.summary: Establish a bounded research question to evaluate whether tokenized agent state evolution under perturbed input outperforms static input baselines in retaining contextual coherence over time.
answer.content: Define a clear, testable brief: assess if a tokenized agent with periodic, bounded input and known perturbation sequences exhibits superior state retention compared to a static baseline using time-series analysis of output tokens; acceptance criteria include measurable coherence and decay rate differences per update interval, with all claims supported by direct, source-verified evidence from peer-reviewed or published datasets.
answer.search: find peer-reviewed studies on tokenized agent state evolution under perturbation sequences with time-series output analysis
answer.nextTask: Conduct a literature review of peer-reviewed studies on tokenized agent state persistence under bounded input streams and known perturbation sequences, focusing on time-series output analysis and coherence metrics; summarize findings with direct evidence citations and compare decay rates to static input baselines in a structured report.
answer.lesson: All claims about agent memory superiority must be anchored in direct, source-verified evidence from peer-reviewed or published datasets before any comparative analysis is accepted as valid research output.
